notes: TBox subject insert under a real class. The worlds only differ on counts (fol), so they carry no axioms. Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30.

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): counts the members of a collection
fol (arithmetic): compares a count with four

fol.notes: Members are numbered: the four listed ones are 1 to 4 (distinct by arithmetic), the two new ones are the constants pellingworth_a and pellingworth_b; membership in the class is a belief (uninterpreted). The edit is the class rule plus the two members it speaks of ('one of the two ... found in 2024'): two different individuals, neither on the old list. Counting needs a closed world: every member the model knows of is a listed one or one of the two new ones (presupposition, what the count rule rests on). w1 stores the figure (number_known), which the edit does not recompute; w2 stores the counting rule over the list (each new member counted once and only if not already listed), so the number follows from the list plus the edit.

listed.says: Four pre-Columbian Maya codices are known to survive: Dresden, Madrid, Paris and Mexico (the list). (stored)

named_only.says: Every member the model knows of is a listed one or one of the two new ones. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(c, Implies(maya_codex(c), Or(And(1 <= c, c <= 4), c == pellingworth_a, c == pellingworth_b)))

stores: number_known(maya_codices) == count(maya_codex(1), maya_codex(2), maya_codex(3), maya_codex(4), And(maya_codex(pellingworth_a), Not(And(1 <= pellingworth_a, pellingworth_a <= 4))), And(maya_codex(pellingworth_b), Not(And(1 <= pellingworth_b, pellingworth_b <= 4)), pellingworth_b != pellingworth_a))
